turns.prompt_text: Water pump, hand-held for less than 1 cm diameter tubes
turns.response_html:
Finding a hand-held pump for tubing smaller than 1 cm (approximately 0.39 inches) requires looking at specialized hobbies, as standard hardware store pumps often use 1/2-inch tubing or larger.

Based on your size constraints, the best options come from the aquarium and homebrewing communities, which rely on precision liquid transfer through small-diameter hoses.

Top Recommendations

1. For Micro Tubing (~3/16" or 5mm)

If you are working with very narrow tubing (standard airline tubing size), the Jellyfish Art Mini Siphon is the most compatible off-the-shelf option. It is designed for delicate tasks like cleaning small tanks without removing too much water quickly.

  • Best For: Precision work, very small volumes, cleaning debris.
  • Tubing Size: 3/16 inch (approx. 4.8 mm).
  • Mechanism: Squeeze bulb or manual siphon action.

Mini Siphon

2. For Standard Small Tubing (~3/8" or 9.5mm)

If your tubing is closer to the 1 cm limit (approx. 9.5mm), the Fermtech Mini Auto-Siphon is the industry standard for homebrewers. It moves liquid faster than the micro options but fits perfectly inside 1-gallon jugs or narrow-neck containers where larger pumps won't fit.

  • Best For: Transferring gallons of liquid, reliable flow, "pumping" to start rather than sucking.
  • Tubing Size: 3/8 inch (approx. 9.5 mm).
  • Mechanism: Piston-based auto-siphon (single stroke starts the flow).

Fermtech Mini Auto-Siphon

Quick Comparison

Community Perspectives & DIY Solutions

Different communities solve the "small tube" problem in unique ways:

  • Aquarium Hobbyists: Often use airline tubing (3/16") to create a slow-flow siphon for cleaning sand in nano-tanks. If you can't find a pump small enough, many hobbyists simply use a 3ml pipette attached to airline tubing to create a manual "micro-pump" for spot cleaning.
  • Homebrewers: Focus on 3/8" tubing to move wine or beer without introducing air bubbles. They prefer "auto-siphons" because they prevent the need to start suction by mouth, which is a contamination risk.
  • Lab/Medical: For extremely precise or sterile transfers (under 3mm), you might look into peristaltic pumps (often battery or electric, not hand-held) which squeeze the tube externally to move fluid.

Video Guide

Using an air hose as a water syphon

The video is relevant because it shows how to effectively move water through tubing significantly smaller than 1 cm without a bulky pump mechanism.

Recommendation: If you need to move liquid up (against gravity), go with the Fermtech Mini as it generates more pressure. If you are draining liquid down, the Jellyfish Art or a simple DIY airline siphon is sufficient.
